searchAudit.objective: Explore executable cooperative-autonomous-driving ideas from control, game-theoretic, and distributed-decision perspectives while excluding cooperative-perception fusion, uncertainty modules, benchmark-only audits, idea scoring, acceptance-threshold inference, and idea-center publication.
rulesApplied: Read config/idea-exploration-workflow.json candidateHardStops before candidate generation.
Read cooperative-autonomous-driving-legacy-ideas-closure-v8.json and fresh-executable-candidate-pool-v9.json before candidate generation.
No candidate score was computed and no acceptance threshold was inferred.
Cooperative-perception fusion, uncertainty gating, and benchmark-audit relabelings were excluded before generation.
A repository or synthetic fault injector was treated only as an execution door, not as evidence that the exact failure naturally occurs.
Candidates requiring a complete CARLA installation or unavailable weights without an independent lightweight falsification path were rejected.
Every candidate was collided against functionally equivalent V2X work and against generic decentralized POMDP, game, control, or multi-robot planning priors.
At most three candidates could survive; an empty shortlist was permitted.

sourceAttempts.result: Read mandatory hard stops, legacy cooperative rejects, the previous v9 candidate pool, and the current cooperative literature review.
Author-submitted primary records were opened for named systems, generic priors, control, games, and runtime assurance.
IEEE author copies, ScienceDirect, AAAI, J-STAGE, and official DOI landing pages were used for metadata and claim checks.
SAE J3186, J3216, J3256 and ETSI TR 103 578 were checked as the maneuver-sharing interoperability baseline.
MDrive, V2Xverse, UrbanV2X, CADET, CommonRoad, and GameFormer project pages were inspected.
Five official repositories were pinned. Two lightweight tests passed, while CARLA, missing LFS objects, SSH-only dependencies, and absent candidate-specific weights blocked task-level closure.

limitations: No public 2023-2026 corpus pairing standardized maneuver-intent messages with realized vehicle actions and natural violation labels was verified.
SwarmDrive exposes a paper but no official code or model release on the arXiv record.
UrbanV2X publishes large ROS bags and calibration, but not maneuver negotiation messages or compact intent-action traces.
MDrive and V2Xverse provide real code and checkpoints but task-level closed-loop evaluation requires CARLA and planner-specific environments.
CommonRoad-Game is advertised as lightweight, but the pinned repository's scenario XML files are unresolved Git LFS pointers and its full dependency list includes SSH GitLab planner URLs.
The passed unit tests establish repository execution only; they are not evidence for a proposed scientific mechanism.

verifiedReferences.title: MDrive: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Cooperative Driving for End-to-End Multi-agent Systems
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Defines 225 closed-loop scenarios and reports that perception gains do not always improve planning and that negotiation can hurt in dense traffic.

verifiedReferences.title: SwarmDrive: Semantic V2V Coordination for Latency-Constrained Cooperative Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.venue: arXiv; submitted to VTC Fall 2026 workshop

verifiedReferences.title: UrbanV2X: A Multisensory Vehicle-Infrastructure Dataset for Cooperative Navigation in Urban Areas

candidateLedger.title: Receiver-side conformance tubes for communicated maneuver intent versus realized action
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A receiver can monitor whether observed motion remains inside the dynamically feasible tube implied by a peer's accepted maneuver commitment and trigger an earlier safe response than state-only collision prediction.
functionalCollision: V2X message-generation rules already trigger updates when a planned trajectory changes.
Intent Sharing in Cooperative Maneuvering already represents intent with dynamical-system bounds and performs conflict analysis.
VERCO already makes cooperative maneuver decisions accountable, while aviation conformance monitoring is a mature generic pattern.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Generic trajectory-conformance monitoring and runtime reachable-set checks already compare intended and realized motion.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The non-generic residual would be a receiver-observable contract tied to J3186 or ETSI maneuver lifecycle, road conflict zones, vehicle braking envelopes, and an accepted right-of-way transfer; generic monitors do not encode that transfer of reliance.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Test-track intent sharing and VERCO show real intent messages and cooperation failures are possible, but no public paired intent-action corpus with natural conformance violations was verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Implement a kinematic tube monitor on a CommonRoad merge scenario and compare state-only TTC, stale-intent, and accepted-intent monitors.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: A public real or test-track trace with both transmitted intent and realized action becomes available and the monitor predicts safety-relevant violations before state-only baselines.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: Only synthetic deviations are available or a standard trajectory-change trigger is functionally equivalent.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would define when a receiver may safely rely on a negotiated trajectory rather than merely treating it as a forecast.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would show that current message-generation rules or state-only monitors are sufficient, preventing an unnecessary contract layer.

candidateLedger.title: Typed diagnosis of strategic reneging versus safety-mandated intent override
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A receiver can separate malicious or strategic reneging from a physically necessary emergency override by checking the sender's declared fallback envelope, observed hazard, and feasible evasive actions.
functionalCollision: Trust-aware resilient CAV control and Byzantine-resilient distributed MPC already bound unsafe peer information.
VERCO records accountable maneuver decisions.
Mission-level runtime assurance already distinguishes rejected commands from executed fallback at one vehicle.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Fault diagnosis and adversarial control already classify model mismatch, faults, and attacks under reachability or residual tests.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The residual requires a V2X-specific distinction between breaking a negotiated right-of-way commitment and exercising a predeclared minimum-risk override that all dependent vehicles must interpret consistently.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: No public V2X maneuver log with labeled strategic reneging and legitimate emergency overrides was verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Use a two-vehicle merge model with declared fallback tubes and pre-registered indistinguishability cases.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: At least one public trace or protocol test exposes both classes and the classifier has nontrivial identifiability beyond speed residuals.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: Labels can only be created by the proposed injector or the two causes are observationally indistinguishable.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would prevent Byzantine defenses from punishing legitimate safety overrides.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: An impossibility result would justify treating intent as nonbinding and always reserving worst-case space.

candidateLedger.title: Two-phase maneuver commitment epochs across asymmetric disconnect and reconnect
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Vehicles should resume a maneuver after reconnection only when both can prove they share the same accepted commitment epoch and fallback state.
functionalCollision: Collaborative Maneuver Protocol already uses distributed state machines, heartbeat, voting rounds, and synchronized transitions.
The 2024 negotiation acceptance scheme adds an agreement phase for participant consistency.
The 2026 cancellation paper implements a complete termination state machine.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Two-phase commit, epochs, leases, and view numbers are mature distributed-systems mechanisms.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The V2X residual would require a physical no-return boundary and a safe occupancy invariant during the period in which peers disagree about the epoch; generic commit protocols do not have moving agents crossing a shared conflict zone.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Asymmetric packet loss and failed coordination are established, but no public reconnect trace with maneuver-epoch divergence was verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Model J3186-like states and a two-vehicle conflict zone in UPPAAL or a compact CommonRoad kinematic model.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: A counterexample exists against the current cancellation or agreement state machines that cannot be removed by a timeout-only policy.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: Heartbeat plus cancellation plus conservative fallback is equivalent.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would add a precise reconnection rule tied to physical commitment boundaries.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would close the need for epochs and support a simpler cancellation-first protocol.

candidateLedger.title: Safety supervisor for the unavoidable disagreement window after asymmetric packet loss
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Instead of requiring immediate protocol agreement, each vehicle maintains a locally computable invariant that remains safe while one peer believes the maneuver is active and another has fallen back.
functionalCollision: The earlier asymmetric-packet-loss literature already identifies necessary disagreement periods and cooperative versus autonomous modes.
RMADER proves recursive feasibility with delayed trajectory publication.
Robust CBF merge control reconciles decentralized disagreement.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Robust invariant sets and Simplex-style fallback are standard control constructions.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The only V2X-specific residue is computing the invariant from a shared maneuver role, conflict-zone geometry, and the last mutually acknowledged trajectory rather than a generic neighbor trajectory.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Packet loss is real, but no matched public execution shows the exact split-brain maneuver state.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Construct a two-vehicle merge automaton and compare timeout, RMADER-style delayed checking, and role-conditioned invariant fallback.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: The role-conditioned invariant admits materially more progress than worst-case fallback while preserving all modeled safety cases.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: A standard robust-CBF or delayed-trajectory baseline is equivalent.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would quantify usable cooperation during unavoidable disagreement.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would support immediate conservative fallback as the only defensible policy.

candidateLedger.title: Physical anti-equivocation for a vehicle sending incompatible intents to different neighbors
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Peers can detect intent equivocation when separately received commitments cannot all be satisfied by one vehicle within its dynamics and road topology.
functionalCollision: VERCO already supplies distributed accountability and verifiable cooperation messages.
Byzantine-resilient platoon control and trust-aware CAV coordination already reject malicious state/control information.
The repository's prior failure-domain quorum direction is blocked and cannot be relabeled.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Authenticated broadcast and equivocation proofs are standard Byzantine-fault-tolerance mechanisms.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The non-generic component would be a physics proof: two individually valid signed intents are jointly impossible because their conflict-zone occupancy and acceleration envelopes cannot coexist.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: No public road or test-track trace of multi-recipient intent equivocation was verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Encode two recipients, one sender, and mutually inconsistent lane-change commitments in a CommonRoad map.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: The physical proof detects attacks that cryptographic duplicate-message checks cannot and has a benign emergency-override rule.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: Only synthetic attacks are available or VERCO-style signed accountability is sufficient.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would provide a V2X-specific Byzantine witness without requiring a global trust score.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would show that physical consistency cannot replace authenticated protocol transcripts.

candidateLedger.title: Strategy-proof merge negotiation with verifiable physical opportunity cost
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A merge mechanism can make truthful urgency or delay-cost reporting optimal by tying allocation and penalties to realized, physically verifiable delay and braking cost.
functionalCollision: Negotiation acceptance schemes already optimize congestion-aware utility.
Decentralized opinion and robust-CBF merge methods already establish orders without private payments.
Older cooperative lane-change bargaining and generic mechanism design already cover transferable utility.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Strategy-proof auctions and dynamic mechanism design already elicit private costs; applying them to a merge is not independently novel.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: A defensible V2X delta would need an observable road-physics payment proxy that cannot be cheaply manipulated by changing trajectory, while preserving emergency priority and mixed nonparticipating traffic.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: No public dataset with private urgency values, bids, and realized cooperative maneuvers was found.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Prove incentive compatibility in a two-lane merge and test manipulations of claimed urgency and controllable approach speed.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: Truthfulness survives trajectory manipulation and emergency-priority constraints with observable quantities only.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: The mechanism requires unverifiable value-of-time or becomes a generic auction instantiation.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would clarify whether truthful negotiation is possible without financial or identity infrastructure.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: An impossibility result would redirect work toward safety-only, non-strategy-proof protocols.

candidateLedger.title: Planner-agnostic occupancy-and-fallback contract for black-box cooperative planners
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Heterogeneous planners can cooperate without sharing internal representations if each exports a time-indexed occupancy tube, commitment deadline, admissible deviation, and fallback tube.
functionalCollision: SAE and ETSI already standardize planned or desired trajectory exchange and maneuver lifecycle.
The prior runtime semantic checker was pilot-negative.
The rolling-model wire-capability direction is active-unresolved and reserved.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Assume-guarantee contracts, interface automata, and trajectory tubes are mature component-interoperability methods.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: A V2X-specific contract must preserve right-of-way transfer, conflict-zone timing, vehicle dynamic feasibility, and an observable fallback despite incompatible GameFormer, CoLMDriver, and classical planner internals.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: MDrive demonstrates cross-paradigm performance differences, but no public cross-planner contract trace or paired black-box checkpoint set is lightweight and complete.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Pair a simple CommonRoad reactive planner with a sampled game planner and test only contract fields, not model internals.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: A minimal field set guarantees compositional collision avoidance and supports nontrivial progress across planner pairs.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: The result is only an interface schema or benchmark matrix.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would identify a planner-independent cooperative boundary rather than another shared model.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would show that planned trajectories alone cannot support safe black-box interoperability.

candidateLedger.title: Cross-planner commitment acceptance using executable capability envelopes
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A receiving planner should accept a proposed maneuver only if its own controller can satisfy the proposal and the sender's declared capability envelope remains compatible with the receiver's fallback.
functionalCollision: J3186 and J3256 already define agreement-seeking and prescriptive merge protocols.
CommonRoad-Autoware and CommonRoad planner interfaces already focus on planner integration.
The active wire-capability direction occupies model and capability negotiation.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Contract-based control and compatibility checking already compose heterogeneous controllers.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The V2X residue is bidirectional physical compatibility between independently owned planners before a shared road maneuver transfers reliance.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: No public dataset identifies failures caused by two different deployed planners interpreting one maneuver contract differently.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Use two lightweight kinematic planners with different horizons and constraints on one CommonRoad merge.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: Capability envelopes predict cross-play failure not captured by trajectory overlap checks.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: The work reduces to schema compatibility or uses synthetic planner differences only.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would give a concrete pre-acceptance interoperability test.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would establish that common occupancy semantics suffice without planner capability exchange.

candidateLedger.title: Road-conflict-aware communication trigger for asymmetric planner beliefs
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Vehicles communicate only when their local belief sets could induce incompatible crossing actions in the same road conflict zone.
functionalCollision: The 2025 Dec-POMDP work directly provides action-consistency guarantees and selective communication under inconsistent beliefs.
Shared Action Suggestions communicates joint actions to reduce belief ambiguity.
Select2Drive and SwarmDrive already trigger V2X communication from decision or uncertainty signals.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: The core problem and intervention are directly covered by recent generic Dec-POMDP work.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: Road conflict zones and stopping feasibility instantiate the action-conflict set, but this is an application-specific constraint rather than a new communication principle.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: MDrive provides broad negotiation harm but not per-agent belief states needed for this test.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Instantiate the generic action-consistency trigger in a two-vehicle intersection POMDP.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: A V2X road invariant changes the guarantee or impossibility boundary rather than only the state space.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: The result is the generic method on a driving scenario.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would connect communication decisions to concrete road conflicts.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would confirm the generic Dec-POMDP trigger is sufficient and avoid duplicate work.

candidateLedger.title: Delay-aware cooperative receding-horizon negotiation with action-history state
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Cooperative planners should augment negotiation state with message age and recent control actions so delayed peer intent remains dynamically interpretable.
functionalCollision: MTCC Part I already augments state with observation delay and action history.
RMADER already introduces delayed trajectory publication checks.
Multi-Uncertainty Aware ACP already includes communication outage constraints in cooperative MPC.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Delay-state augmentation and receding-horizon robust control are standard methods.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The V2X-specific aspect is a peer's communicated future maneuver, but the proposed state augmentation is already present in CAV control work.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Communication delay is well evidenced, so occurrence is not the blocker.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Implement a small platoon or merge MPC with delayed intent and action history.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: A new commitment-level invariant appears beyond existing MTCC and RMADER guarantees.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Could clarify when intent history outperforms status history.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would support existing MTCC and intent-reconstruction baselines.

candidateLedger.title: Formally verified fallback from agreement-seeking to autonomous mode
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A finite-state maneuver protocol and continuous vehicle dynamics can be composed to verify that every communication failure transition reaches a collision-free autonomous fallback.
functionalCollision: CommonUppRoad already converts CommonRoad scenarios to UPPAAL for formal verification.
Mission-level runtime assurance and Safe-RMM already implement executable monitoring and fallback or shielding.
The asymmetric-packet-loss and Collaborative Maneuver Protocol work already define cooperative and autonomous modes with failure handling.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Hybrid automata, runtime assurance, and Simplex fallback are mature formal-control methods.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The V2X residue is verifying a distributed maneuver-state transition under asymmetric receipt while vehicles physically approach a no-return boundary.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Communication loss is natural, but no public executable maneuver protocol model with synchronized vehicle dynamics was verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Encode a two-vehicle merge protocol in UPPAAL and replay the resulting timing bounds in a CommonRoad kinematic scenario.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: The composition exposes a new unsafe protocol transition or a nontrivial safe timing bound absent from protocol-only and controller-only analyses.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: It merely demonstrates CommonUppRoad or Simplex on another scenario.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would produce an executable cross-layer counterexample or certified timing envelope.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would show the protocol adds no safety risk beyond existing worst-case fallback assumptions.

candidateLedger.title: Safe reacquisition after maneuver cancellation and peer reappearance
candidateLedger.coreClaim: After cancellation or disappearance, a returning peer should be treated as a new participant until its current feasible tube is re-established, preventing stale continuation of the old maneuver.
functionalCollision: The 2026 cancellation paper directly defines how unsuitable coordination ends.
Trajectory message generation rules already require updates on meaningful plan change.
Generic lease and session-restart protocols already invalidate stale state.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Session epochs and stale-state invalidation are standard distributed-systems mechanisms.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The road-specific residue is a physical reacquisition guard based on whether the returning vehicle can still honor the old conflict-zone allocation.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: No public maneuver trace with loss, cancellation, reconnection, and realized trajectories was verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Extend the public cancellation state machine with physical re-entry guards in a compact merge model.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: A stale-session counterexample survives all existing cancellation and timeout rules.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: Treating every reconnect as a fresh negotiation is already sufficient.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would make the reconnect semantics explicit and physically grounded.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would validate the simpler fresh-negotiation rule.

candidateLedger.title: Physics-feasibility filter plus local safety shield for Byzantine maneuver intent
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A vehicle can reject communicated intents that are dynamically infeasible and use a CBF shield against feasible but malicious intents.
functionalCollision: Byzantine-resilient distributed MPC already handles malicious connected-vehicle platoon information.
Trust-aware resilient CAV control already estimates and reacts to untrustworthy peers.
RSR-RSMARL and Safe-RMM already use local CBF shields with communication.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Model-validity filters followed by robust safety shields are a standard defense composition.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: A V2X-specific method would need to exploit maneuver-role obligations, not merely physical feasibility, because a malicious but feasible trajectory can still violate an accepted right-of-way transfer.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Byzantine attacks are studied in platoons, but no public maneuver-negotiation attack trace and matched checkpoint were verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Use a compact intersection controller with feasible deceptive GO and YIELD messages.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: Role-obligation features detect attacks missed by dynamics-only filters and improve safety-efficiency over worst-case shielding.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: The CBF alone handles all cases or only injected attacks support the claim.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would identify the safety gap between physical feasibility and negotiated compliance.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would support local shielding without a new Byzantine negotiation layer.

candidateLedger.title: Causal attribution of MDrive negotiation harm to message-action mismatch
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Dense-traffic negotiation failures in MDrive can be decomposed into misleading messages, planner interpretation errors, and downstream control deviations.
functionalCollision: MDrive already analyzes negotiation failures across closed-loop scenarios.
The prior candidate pool rejected matched-scene planning-harm and benchmark-diagnostic candidates.
The requested scope forbids benchmark audit as the contribution.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Causal trace attribution and component ablation are standard system-diagnosis methods.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: Only the explicit message-to-waypoint-to-actuation chain is V2X-specific, but extracting it would remain an evaluation protocol unless it yields a new intervention.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: MDrive provides natural closed-loop failure evidence, but not a lightweight public execution path on the current machine.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Instrument CoLMDriver negotiation outputs, waypoints, and controls on the MDrive interaction subset.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: A reusable intervention follows from a stable failure mechanism.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: The output is only a taxonomy, benchmark slice, or CARLA-dependent audit.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Could identify where negotiation causes action harm.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Could rule out message-action mismatch and redirect work toward planner robustness.

candidateLedger.title: Minimal sufficient semantics for planner-to-planner cross-play
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A controlled cross-play study can identify the smallest shared intent fields needed for classical, learned game-theoretic, and language-negotiation planners to cooperate safely.
functionalCollision: SAE and ETSI already define interoperable maneuver message content.
GameFormer, V2Xverse, and CoLMDriver expose materially different planner representations but do not expose a common lightweight checkpoint suite.
The prior runtime semantic checker and wire-capability directions occupy schema and capability validation.
candidateLedger.genericPriorCollision: Interface minimization and cross-play matrices are standard interoperability evaluations.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: The V2X difference is cross-vendor transfer of reliance for one physical road conflict, but a field-ablation matrix alone is still a benchmark audit.
candidateLedger.naturalEvidence: Heterogeneous planners exist, yet public matched checkpoints and a compact shared scenario runner were not verified.

twoWeekGoNoGo.plan: Adapter-based pairwise tests among a classical planner, a GameFormer-like planner, and a negotiation policy.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: The study yields a formal sufficiency or impossibility result, not only ranking.
twoWeekGoNoGo.noGoCondition: Unavailable weights, full CARLA dependence, or benchmark-only output.

candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would define a portable cooperative planner interface.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would show no compact shared semantics are sufficient without exposing planner internals.

mechanicalReasons: No public naturally occurring intent-action violation corpus was verified.
The remaining monitor is a generic conformance method applied to a V2X contract.
The two target causes are not labeled in any verified public V2X trace.
A synthetic injector would prove testability only.
Distributed state machines, agreement phases, heartbeat, cancellation, and epochs are already functionally occupied.
No natural reconnect divergence trace was verified.
Asymmetric disagreement and robust fallback are established prior problems.
The proposed invariant is a standard robust-control transfer without a verified new V2X boundary.
No public equivocation occurrence evidence was verified.
VERCO and existing Byzantine control occupy accountability and malicious-peer handling, while the candidate lacks a matched asset.
Private utility and truthful-report labels are unavailable.
Without a new manipulation-proof physical observable, this is generic mechanism design applied to merging.
Contract and trajectory semantics overlap standards and prior rejected semantic-checker work.
No lightweight heterogeneous checkpoint suite was verified.
Capability negotiation collides with an active reserved wire-capability direction.
Synthetic planner incompatibility is not natural occurrence evidence.
Recent Dec-POMDP work directly covers action consistency with inconsistent beliefs and selective communication.
Road conflict zones merely instantiate the generic action-conflict set.
MTCC, RMADER, and multi-uncertainty cooperative MPC directly cover the proposed state and control mechanisms.
CommonUppRoad, runtime assurance, CBF shielding, and cooperative/autonomous protocol modes occupy the method stack.
The exact distributed model is not publicly executable.
Fresh negotiation after reconnect is already a sufficient standard baseline unless a natural stale-session counterexample is shown.
No such trace was verified.
Dynamics filters plus CBF shields are a generic defense composition and direct CAV Byzantine-control priors exist.
Only injected maneuver attacks would be available.
The task-level path requires full CARLA and planner environments.
The remaining output is a prohibited benchmark audit or diagnostic taxonomy.
GameFormer lacks released weights in its official repository and V2Xverse/MDrive require heavy CARLA stacks.
Field-ablation cross-play without a formal result is benchmark-only and overlaps prior semantic/wire work.

conclusion.summary: No candidate simultaneously retains a V2X-specific novelty residual beyond decentralized POMDP, game, distributed-systems, or robust-control priors; has natural evidence for the exact failure; has a pinned public asset that exercises the same semantic object without a full CARLA stack or unavailable weights; and supports a two-week go/no-go with useful positive and negative outcomes.
strongestResiduals: Receiver-side intent-action conformance tied to an accepted right-of-way transfer, but it lacks a public natural violation corpus and risks being generic conformance monitoring.
Distinguishing strategic reneging from a legitimate emergency override, but the causes are not identifiable from any verified public V2X trace.
A physical anti-equivocation witness for mutually impossible signed intents, but only synthetic attacks and no matched public execution asset are available.
dominantEliminationReasons: Direct functional coverage by J3186/ETSI maneuver lifecycle work, acceptance consistency, cancellation, RMADER, recent action-consistency Dec-POMDPs, robust CBF negotiation, VERCO, and Byzantine-resilient platoon control.
The exact message-action, reconnect, strategic-reporting, and equivocation failures are injectable but not evidenced in public natural or test-track releases.

MDrive and V2Xverse task-level experiments require CARLA and planner-specific stacks; GameFormer lacks released weights; CommonRoad-Game has unresolved LFS scenario objects and SSH-only planner dependencies.
Several remaining outputs would be an interoperability matrix, schema checker, causal benchmark audit, or generic formal-method transfer, all excluded by the run rules.
